Japan fired anti-ship missiles from Philippine soil for the first time in the post-World War II era during Balikatan 2026. On May 6, the Japan Self-Defense Forces launched two Type 88 surface-to-ship missiles from Paoay, Ilocos Norte, hitting the decommissioned BRP Quezon about 75 kilometers offshore in the South China Sea. The launch was part of a maritime strike drill involving Filipino, Japanese, and allied forces.

The live-fire exercise came after the Philippines and Japan ratified a reciprocal access agreement in 2025, allowing closer military cooperation between the two countries. Around 1,400 Japanese troops joined Balikatan, which ran from April 20 to May 8 and involved about 17,000 personnel from seven countries. Philippine Navy officials said the country continues to build a layered coastal defense system, while AFP officials welcomed support from like-minded nations amid discussions on the possible transfer of Japan’s Type 88 missile system to Manila.
